issues.display_title: Issue #1724: [Linting] Resolve TypeScript quality findings in pages and feature areas
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Page and feature code contains the largest share of the current TypeScript lint backlog. The audit found 85 affected files with 423 errors and 673 warnings.

This work should be delivered incrementally by feature area so changes remain reviewable and can be tested without mixing unrelated user flows.

Scope

  • Resolve TypeScript lint findings under the pages and feature areas.
  • Prioritize unsafe or correctness-related findings before style warnings.
  • Replace loose types progressively with meaningful domain types.
  • Remove unused code and correct equality checks.
  • Preserve user-visible behavior.
  • Split delivery into small pull requests grouped by feature or route.

Suggested delivery order

  1. Small and low-risk pages.
  2. Settings and account flows.
  3. Pricing and payment flows.
  4. Gallery management flows.
  5. Virtual gallery editor areas.

Acceptance criteria

  • Each completed feature area has no TypeScript lint errors.
  • The final pages area has no TypeScript lint errors.
  • Remaining warnings, if any, are documented and narrowly justified.
  • No blanket rule disabling is introduced.
  • Behavior-sensitive changes include appropriate tests.
  • Affected user flows are smoke-tested.
  • The Angular development build succeeds after each pull request.

Out of scope

  • Shared components and shared services.
  • Template accessibility findings.
  • Lint configuration or severity changes.

Notes

This is intentionally one roadmap issue with multiple small pull requests. Avoid a single repository-wide cleanup pull request.

issues.display_title: Issue #1725: [Linting] Resolve TypeScript quality findings in shared services
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Shared services sit on critical data, upload, API, and utility paths. The current audit found 9 affected service files with 15 errors and 133 warnings, mostly loose types, equality checks, and unused code.

Because service changes can affect many screens, the cleanup should emphasize stable contracts and regression protection.

Scope

  • Resolve TypeScript lint findings under the shared services area.
  • Introduce meaningful request, response, state, and callback types.
  • Remove unused code only after confirming it has no consumers.
  • Correct equality checks without changing data-handling behavior.
  • Add focused tests around high-risk service changes.

Acceptance criteria

  • Shared service TypeScript files have no lint errors.
  • Public service contracts remain compatible or all consumers are updated together.
  • Remaining warnings, if any, are explicitly justified and narrowly suppressed.
  • No blanket rule disabling is introduced.
  • Upload, API, and state-related behavior remains unchanged.
  • Relevant unit tests pass.
  • The Angular development build succeeds.

Out of scope

  • Components and pages.
  • Template accessibility findings.
  • General lint configuration changes.

issues.display_title: Issue #1726: [Linting] Align Angular component APIs with current conventions
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

The lint audit identified Angular-specific issues such as event outputs using the "on" prefix, components without the project selector prefix, and empty lifecycle methods.

These findings affect the consistency and maintainability of component APIs. Some fixes may touch multiple consumers, so they should be handled as deliberate compatibility updates rather than mechanical renames.

Scope

  • Rename event outputs that do not follow Angular conventions.
  • Align component selectors with the project's naming convention where practical.
  • Remove empty lifecycle methods and unnecessary lifecycle declarations.
  • Update every affected template and TypeScript consumer.
  • Preserve public behavior and emitted event semantics.

Acceptance criteria

  • Angular-specific TypeScript lint errors are resolved.
  • All renamed outputs and selectors are updated at every call site.
  • Components continue to emit the same data at the same user interactions.
  • Empty lifecycle methods are removed unless a documented reason requires them.
  • No broad lint suppression is added.
  • Relevant unit tests pass.
  • The Angular development build succeeds.
  • Affected UI flows are smoke-tested.

Out of scope

  • General TypeScript cleanup unrelated to Angular APIs.
  • Template accessibility findings.
  • Lint configuration changes.

Notes

Coordinate this task with the area-based cleanup issues to avoid duplicate edits. If an API is already corrected in an area cleanup, record it here instead of changing it twice.

issues.display_title: Issue #1727: [Accessibility] Resolve Angular template lint findings
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

The lint audit found 169 accessibility-related errors across Angular templates. The largest groups involve labels that are not connected to controls, mouse interactions without keyboard support, interactive elements that cannot receive focus, and images without alternative text.

These are user-facing accessibility gaps and should be fixed based on the intended interaction, not by silencing the checks.

Scope

  • Associate form labels with the correct controls.
  • Ensure custom clickable elements are keyboard accessible or replace them with native controls.
  • Ensure interactive elements can receive focus.
  • Add meaningful alternative text or correctly mark decorative images.
  • Review affected interactions for accessible names, roles, and states.
  • Add focused tests where interaction behavior changes.

Acceptance criteria

  • Angular HTML templates have no accessibility lint errors.
  • Form controls have correctly associated labels or accessible names.
  • Every interactive action can be completed with a keyboard.
  • Focus behavior is visible and logical.
  • Images have appropriate alternative text treatment.
  • Native HTML elements are preferred where they provide the required behavior.
  • No blanket accessibility-rule suppression is added.
  • Affected flows are keyboard smoke-tested.
  • The Angular development build succeeds.

Out of scope

  • Visual redesign.
  • General TypeScript lint cleanup.
  • Changing the accessibility rule set to hide existing findings.

Notes

Work by screen or feature so each pull request can be reviewed and tested as a complete user interaction.

issues.display_title: Issue #1728: [Linting] Enable type-aware checks and enforce linting in CI
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Final step of the linting roadmap: enable deeper TypeScript checks and make linting an automated quality gate.

Delivered. The gate is a local pre-commit hook, and type-aware linting is enabled for a defined set of rules, all of which are clear. The no-unsafe-* family and two promise rules were measured and deliberately left off; the numbers are recorded at the bottom so the work can be picked up later.

Decision: no GitHub Actions (2026-07-29)

GitHub Actions is not to be used on this repository, and no check may run on pull request or on push. Actions is disabled here in any case — GET /repos/GoThruMedia/villume-admin/actions/permissions returns {"enabled": false}.

The gate is therefore a local pre-commit hook (husky + lint-staged), delivered in #1741. What that deliberately gives up, recorded so it is not mistaken for an oversight:

  • It is bypassable with git commit --no-verify.
  • It only sees the files staged in one commit, never the repository as a whole.
  • It cannot be made a required check on a protected branch.
  • Unlike a CI job it does modify files: eslint --fix and prettier --write run and restage, so the corrected version is what gets committed.

Whole-repository verification stays manual: pnpm lint and pnpm format:check, documented in the README.

What was delivered

PR Change
#1741 husky + lint-staged pre-commit hook; qa_testing/ excluded from ESLint; dead @types/jasminewd2 removed
#1742 projectService enabled, plus await-thenable, no-base-to-string, no-redundant-type-constituents, no-unnecessary-type-assertion, only-throw-error — 33 findings cleared
#1743 require-await — 16 findings cleared
#1744 no-explicit-any turned off by decision — 915 warnings down to 8
#1745 no-misused-promises — 16 findings cleared

development is at 0 lint errors, 8 warnings, all no-console.

Type-aware rules now enforced

await-thenable                  no-misused-promises
no-base-to-string               no-redundant-type-constituents
no-unnecessary-type-assertion   only-throw-error
require-await

The recommendedTypeChecked preset is not extended. Rules are enabled individually so the tree can be kept at zero errors, which is what "checks that can be kept green" required.

Real bugs fixed along the way

  • exhibition-uploader built both upload requests as new Promise(async (resolve, reject) => { await ... }). If building the payload threw, the returned promise stayed pending forever and the upload hung silently. (#1745)
  • promocode-form used async ngOnInit(). Angular discards the returned promise, so a failure left isFetching stuck on. (#1745)
  • Async subscribe callbacks dropped their rejections. In edit-image, that skipped enableLoading(false) and left the editor blocked behind the loading overlay until reload. Fourteen such sites now route the rejection to the same place a failed request goes. (#1745)
  • data.interceptor rethrew { ...error }, a plain spread of HttpErrorResponse, which drops the prototype so instanceof never matched downstream. (#1742)
  • editor.service awaited getCameraYPosition, which returns number | null. (#1742)
  • @types/jasminewd2 redeclared every jasmine matcher as returning Promise<void>, making ordinary assertions look like unhandled promises. Removing it eliminated 173 phantom findings. (#1741)

Acceptance criteria

  • Type-aware linting is enabled for a defined set of rules, listed above, and all of them are clear.
  • Every finding from an enabled rule is resolved. One suppression exists, on a single line, with a stated reason: HttpErrorResponse implements Error but does not extend it, so only-throw-error cannot see it as throwable.
  • Linting passes locally — pnpm lint reports 0 errors.
  • A pre-commit hook runs linting and formatting over the staged files.
  • A lint error blocks the commit; the warning baseline is documented rather than enforced.
  • The hook installs itself on pnpm install, so a new clone is covered without extra steps.
  • The team has documented whole-repository commands (pnpm lint, pnpm format:check) in the README.
  • The Angular development build succeeds.
  • No blanket rule disabling is introduced.

Dropped, because they describe a CI job that will not exist:

  • CI runs linting for pull requests and protected branches.
  • CI fails when new lint errors are introduced.
  • The lint job does not modify files. Inverted by design: the hook fixes and restages what it can.

Deferred, to be picked up later

Measured on development at 2db639d93 by enabling each rule temporarily and reverting. Not filed separately yet.

Rule Findings Nature
no-unsafe-member-access 4419 downstream of any
no-unsafe-assignment 2247 downstream of any
no-unsafe-call 1782 downstream of any
no-unsafe-argument 302 downstream of any
no-unsafe-return 140 downstream of any
no-unsafe-* subtotal 8890
no-floating-promises 189 per-site decision
prefer-promise-reject-errors 62 mechanical
no-console 8 leftover debug logging

The no-unsafe-* family is a typing project, not a lint pass. Those 8890 are not 8890 separate problems — they are roughly 900 any annotations counted once per member access, call, assignment, argument and return downstream of each. Turning no-explicit-any off in #1744 removed the reports about the annotations but changed no types, and the count did not move: 8892 before, 8890 after. Only writing real types will clear them. Babylon.js is the largest single blocker; it is annotated as any with a comment throughout.

The other 259 are tractable whenever someone picks them up, smallest first: no-console (8 — six are leftover debug logging, two are legitimate Express boot messages in server.ts that want a config exception), then prefer-promise-reject-errors (62), then no-floating-promises (189), which is where the remaining promise-handling bugs live.

Out of scope

  • Unrelated framework upgrades.
  • Reformatting the entire repository.
  • Adding checks that cannot be kept green by the team.
  • GitHub Actions, and any check triggered by a pull request or a push.
